oracle_output.summary: Site-wide visual overhaul implementing a 4-tier elevation system, typography ladder, shadow tokens, chart standardization with shared color constants, Launchpad redesign with hero banner and premium treatments, and layout improvements including sidebar active states and page transitions.
key_claims: Added 4-tier opaque surface elevation system: bg < panel < card < elevated with corresponding CSS classes
Created CHART constants object with BID/ASK/CYAN/BLUE/GRID/LABEL color values for SVG contexts
Standardized all 5 chart components (DepthChart, VolumeProfile, Heatmap, PriceChart, OrderBook) to use shared CHART constants
Unified candle-down color to #EF4444 across charts and added tabular-nums class to number spans
Added shadow tokens (elevation-1/2/3, glow-cyan/blue) and micro-interactions (.hover-lift, .press-down)
Redesigned Sidebar with left-bar cyan accent for active states, replacing dot indicators
Added brand lockup with gradient glow and section separators in Sidebar
Implemented page transition animation on route change in AppLayout with .page-enter class
Redesigned Launchpad with hero banner featuring gradient background, pulsing status dot, and live metrics
Added premium treatment to LaunchCardMini with top-edge gradient, hover scale+shadow, and gradient quality bar
Upgraded .btn component with focus-visible ring and active scale transform
Migrated RLMF tabs from hardcoded hex values to design system tokens
Added staggered card entrance animation with 40ms delay increments
oracle_output.follow_up_question: What color value did the `candle-down` color get unified to in the chart standardization, replacing the previous `#FB7185`?
oracle_output.follow_up_response:
Based on the diff content, the `candle-down` color was unified to `#EF4444`, replacing the previous `#FB7185`.

This can be seen in the PriceChart.tsx file where the color assignment was changed from:
```typescript
const color = isUp ? '#4ADE80' : '#FB7185';
```

to:
```typescript
const color = isUp ? CHART.BID : CHART.ASK;
```

And in the constants/colors.ts file, `CHART.ASK` is defined as `'#EF4444'` with the comment indicating it corresponds to `echelon-red`.
